meta.name: English
meta.note: The FIRST entry in 'choices' is the correct answer — the game shuffles them at run time. 'why' is the explanation; 'act' is the real teardown step shown on a correct boss answer.

gate.q: How many ports does the hub have for parts?
gate.why: The Large Hub has six ports, A through F. Any port works, but it must match the one written in your program.

gate.q: Which pin colour do you use to lock something firmly?
gate.why: Black and blue friction pins have a rough surface and grip = locking. Light grey and beige frictionless pins are smooth and turn = rotation.
The Distance Sensor measures how far away an object is using ultrasound. The two eye-like holes are also LEDs you can switch on and off.

mission.q: Your program says "motor A". Which port takes the cable?
mission.why: The port in the program and the port you actually used must match. If nothing moves, check this first!

mission.q: The build is done but the motor won't move. What do you check first?
choices: The cable and the port letter
mission.why: Nine times out of ten the cable is loose or the port is wrong. The run button is the next thing to check.

boss.q: Time to take it apart. What comes off first?
boss.why: Start with the cable, the part carrying electricity. Go ahead and unplug it now!

boss.q: What is the right way to unplug a cable?
choices: Hold the hard plug and pull
boss.why: Pulling the wire snaps the strands inside. Always hold the plug.

boss.q: A black friction pin is stuck fast. What do you do?
choices: Lever it out with the separator
Pick at it with your nails
boss.why: Friction pins are meant to be hard to remove. The separator saves your fingers and the parts.

boss.q: What is the correct teardown order?
choices: The reverse of how you built it
boss.why: Reverse order is fastest and safest. Finally, sort the parts back into their trays — that's courtesy to the next person.
